title: What counts as magic
md:
**Question.** What did the texts call magic, and what did they set it against: religion, science, fraud or heresy? This covers magia against goeteia, natural against demonic magic, and the definitions of Frazer, Tylor and Mauss.

**Answer.** The premodern texts have no neutral word for magic. They have pairs of words, and each pair carries a verdict. The verdict usually belongs to an accuser, and the accuser's word is the one that survived. Modern scholarship then turned that word into a neutral category. The full verdict table is in `research/does-magic-translate.md`.

## The Greek pairs

The Greek vocabulary is already split:
- **mageia** invokes benevolent daemons for some good;
- **goeteia** belongs to tombs and wailing, and to chthonic phantoms;
- **pharmakeia** is a deadly potion [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lexw-suda-goeteia-mageia-pharmakeia) [[2]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lexw-psellus-goeteia-chthonic-phantoms).

Gorgias already calls both mageia and goeteia "errors of the soul and deceptions of opinion" [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#lexw-gorgias-goeteia-mageia-errors). Theurgy claims a place above both: it is ritual that acts, not thought [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lat-iamblichus-theurgy-not-thought).

## The Christian collapse

The Christian accusers refused the split:
- Augustine reports the distinction between goetia and theurgy and rejects it, because both are demonic [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lat-augustine-magic-goetia-theurgy-one).
- Peucer reports the pagan distinction and then overrules it: all mageia comes from the Devil [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexw-peucer-mageia-collapsed-into-goeteia).
- Bodin's Latin uses *magus* for the French *sorcier*, so no lawful magus is left [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexw-bodin-latin-magus-for-sorcier) [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-bodin-sorcerer-definition).

Several Latin neighbours of *magia* are not words for magic at all:
- *praestigium* is illusion, a blinding of the eyes [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#lexw-isidore-praestigium-blinds-eyes);
- *superstitio* is worship in excess or misdirected [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#lexw-aquinas-superstitio-excess);
- *maleficium* is evil-doing that the Malleus turns into a heresy [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexw-malleus-malefic-name).

Pliny's "most fraudulent of arts" takes its force from absorbing medicine, religion and astrology [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#anc-pliny-magic-triple-bond).

## The defenders' reply

The defenders took the Greek split back:
- Pico keeps *mageia* for the highest knowledge and leaves goeteia for the demonic [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#lexw-pico-greeks-goeteia-mageia).
- Naudé sorts magic into divine, theurgic, goetic and natural [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexw-naude-four-magicks).
- The Arbatel sets the Magus against the Cacomagus [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/grimoire#grim-arbatel-magus-cacomagus).
- Del Rio widens *magia* on purpose, so that it includes natural magic, and defines it by a created, non-supernatural power [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-delrio-magic-definition) [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-delrio-includes-natural).
- Porta makes natural magic "the practical part of natural philosophy" [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-porta-definition).

## Against what, after 1750

Magic stopped being set against true religion and started being set against true science:
- Bekker [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-bekker-no-sorcery) and Hume [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-hume-miracles-barbarous) treat it as error;
- Tylor [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-tylor-association-of-ideas) [[22]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-primitive-science-vs-hidden-virtues) treats it as mistaken science;
- Hubert and Mauss, through Doutté, treat it as a collective creation [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-doutte-collective-creation) [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-social-vs-pact).

Page 10 has the full sequence.

## Claims

- Greek: [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#lexw-gorgias-goeteia-mageia-errors) [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lexw-suda-goeteia-mageia-pharmakeia) [[2]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lexw-psellus-goeteia-chthonic-phantoms) [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lat-iamblichus-theurgy-not-thought)
- Latin and Christian: [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lat-augustine-magic-goetia-theurgy-one) [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexw-peucer-mageia-collapsed-into-goeteia) [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#lexw-isidore-praestigium-blinds-eyes) [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#lexw-aquinas-superstitio-excess) [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexw-malleus-malefic-name) [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#anc-pliny-magic-triple-bond)
- Renaissance: [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#lexw-pico-greeks-goeteia-mageia) [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexw-naude-four-magicks) [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/grimoire#grim-arbatel-magus-cacomagus) [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-porta-definition)
- French and German: [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexw-bodin-latin-magus-for-sorcier) [[25]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#lexw-martius-magos-wise-vs-zauberey) [[26]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-thomasius-carolina-109)
- Modern: [[27]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-error-vs-real-power) [[22]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-primitive-science-vs-hidden-virtues) [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-social-vs-pact)

## Critiques

- Whose label "magic" is matters (standing critique 4). Otto weights polemical and self-descriptive uses equally ◐ [[28]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-otto-magie-2011). Styers argues the boundary is policed to secure modern identity ◐ [[29]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-styers-making-magic).
- Bailey asks what the grand definitions are still good for ◐ [[30]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-bailey-meanings) [[31]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#hist-bailey-classic-definitions-narrower-studies).

## Open questions

- Does any pre-1700 text on the shelf use *magia* neutrally, as a descriptive category, without a verdict? Del Rio comes closest, and he is an inquisitor.
- Is *Hexerei* defined anywhere on the shelf, as distinct from *Zauberei*?
- Several SL translations render *veneficium*, *maleficium* and Μάγος with the accuser's sense (`research/does-magic-translate.md`). Should SL's translation prompt keep the native term in brackets?

title: Beyond Europe
md:
**Question.** Does "magic" exist outside Europe? This covers Arabic siḥr and the science of letters, Jewish magic, Indic tantra and mantra, Daoist talismans and Tibetan ritual.

**Answer.** No tradition we checked has one neutral word for magic. Each has a split, and the line falls in a different place in each:

| Tradition | Where the line falls |
|---|---|
| Arabic | the miracle's source and its challenge |
| Hebrew | the deed, not the illusion |
| Indic | the victim, not the technique |
| Chinese | orthodoxy, judged by the state |
| Tibetan | no illicit class at all |

Many of the English "magic"s on the shelf are a translator's word. The verdicts are in `research/does-magic-translate.md`.

## Arabic

*Siḥr* is the nearest umbrella. The practitioner's manual defines it neutrally, as whatever has a cause hidden from most minds [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-picatrix-magic-hidden-cause). It then subdivides the art into *nīranj*, the talisman and alchemy [[2]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-picatrix-three-subjects).

The theologian draws the decisive line. Ibn Khaldūn separates three things by the challenge (*taḥaddī*) the prophet issues in advance:
- the prophet's miracle;
- the saint's *karāma*;
- the sorcerer's *siḥr* [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-khaldun-miracle-vs-sorcery).

Lane reports that common usage makes *siḥr* satanic, and splits spiritual magic into divine and satanic kinds [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-lane-sehr-satanic) [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-lane-rohani-divine-satanic). Ibn Khaldūn's treatment of the science of letters as *sīmiyāʾ* is recalled, not yet read ○ [unverified].

## Hebrew

The *mekhashef*, liable to death, is the one who performs a real deed, not the one who seizes the eyes [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#jew-mishnah-sorcerer-deed-not-illusion). The Talmud grades the acts like Sabbath law [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#jew-talmud-witchcraft-like-sabbath-law). Maimonides is read as separating demonic magic, punished by stoning, from sleight of hand, punished by lashes [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#jew-maimonides-two-kinds-magic-commentary).

The practitioner's own heading is *segullah*, a working remedy "by the help of the Blessed Name" [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#lexw-gaster-segulah-heading).

## Indic

Healing and appeasing rites (*bheṣaja*, *śānti*) stand against hostile ones (*abhicāra*, *kṛtyā*). Bloomfield finds witchcraft judged useful or noxious "only according to whom it is turned against" [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-av-witchcraft-blended) [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-av-yatu-fourth-veda).

Manu fines root-rites (*mūlakarman*) and *kṛtyā* used against strangers. His commentators allow root-rites against a husband or a relative [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-manu-mulakarman-krtya-abhicara). The six acts put hostile and peaceful rites in one programme [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-satkarman-mahodadhi) [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-satkarman-sharada).

Two words are not magic words, despite the English:
- *māyā* is a god's praised power of illusion [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-sayana-maya-indra);
- *siddhi* is attainment [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-woodroffe-siddhi-result).

The *vidyāḥ* of the Kathāsaritsāgara become "magic sciences" only in SL's English [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-kathasarit-vidya-magic-sciences).

## Tibetan

This is the counter-case. Pacifying (*zhi*), increasing (*rgyas*), subjugating (*dbang*) and fierce (*drag*) are four sanctioned activities. The fierce rite is done after offerings and with the gurus' permission. It is not a crime [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-thadrak-four-activities) [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-tengyur-firewood-activities) [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-tengyur-drag-po-las-mantra) [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-toh2002-seven-wrathful-rites) [[22]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-tibet-torma-zor).

## Chinese

The line is orthodox against heterodox, and the labels belong to the state and the literati:
- The words for the forbidden arts are *yao* and *xie* ("methods of demonry"). They take in harmless heterodox rites too [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-degroot-yaoshu-xieshu).
- *Wugu* is a capital charge at court, in Han China in 91 BCE and in Korea in 1701 [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-degroot-wugu-91bce) [[25]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-kinyon-wugu-1701) [[26]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-degroot-ku-law).
- The state's offence is "deluding the multitude" [[27]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-zishi-zuoci-huozhong) [[28]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-zishi-wu-heterodox-execution).

The *wu* themselves held offices [[29]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-degroot-wu-offices), and Winkelman argues they were better called ritualists ◐ [[30]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-winkelman-wu-ritualist). Talismans (*fu*) are licit tools of the Daoist canon [[31]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-daozang-fu-white-silk). *Gu* runs from a medical poison to seduction and decay [[32]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-zhubing-gu-definition) [[33]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-peiwen-gu-semantic-range).

## Japanese

On the shelf, 呪術 is a Buddhist dhāraṇī incantation, and so is licit [[34]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-siyi-zhoushu-dharani) [[35]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-eitel-atharva-zhoushu). Its modern use as the academic word for "magic" is recalled, not read ○ [unverified]. The shelf's onmyōdō is court astrology [[36]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-joly-seimei-court-astrologer).

## Claims

- Arabic: [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-picatrix-magic-hidden-cause) [[2]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-picatrix-three-subjects) [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-khaldun-miracle-vs-sorcery) [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-lane-sehr-satanic) [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-lane-rohani-divine-satanic)
- Hebrew: [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#jew-mishnah-sorcerer-deed-not-illusion) [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#jew-talmud-witchcraft-like-sabbath-law) [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#jew-maimonides-two-kinds-magic-commentary) [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#lexw-gaster-segulah-heading)
- Indic: [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#asi-av-witchcraft-blended) [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-manu-mulakarman-krtya-abhicara) [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-sayana-maya-indra) [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-woodroffe-siddhi-result) [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-kathasarit-vidya-magic-sciences)
- Tibetan: [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-thadrak-four-activities) [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-toh2002-seven-wrathful-rites)
- Chinese: [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-degroot-yaoshu-xieshu) [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-degroot-wugu-91bce) [[25]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-kinyon-wugu-1701) [[27]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-zishi-zuoci-huozhong) [[37]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-soushen-huanshu)
- Japanese: [[34]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-siyi-zhoushu-dharani) [[35]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-eitel-atharva-zhoushu) [[38]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/asian#lexa-kanze-majinai-not-in-original)

## Critiques

- Muchowska asks whether "magic", a Western category, still fits Daoist healing rites (*zhuyou*) ◐ [[39]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexa-crit-muchowska-magic-sinology).
- Most of the Chinese evidence comes through de Groot, a Western sinologist who sorts it into "sorcery" and "magic". His categories are a translator's, and should be read as such.
- The shelf is mostly European print (standing critique 6). The Japanese evidence is thin, and the Japanese texts on the shelf are mostly in Western languages.

## Open questions

- Manu XI.33 (the Atharvan as a Brahmin's weapon) is recalled only ○ [unverified]. If it holds, the same rite is a crime for one caste and a weapon for another.
- Where does *zuodao* (左道) appear as a legal term? Neither it nor the Kauśika Sūtra is on the shelf.
- The *majinai* in SL's English of the Kanze utaibon is not in the Japanese. It should be checked against the page image.

title: Revival and its historians
md:
**Question.** Lévi, spiritualism and the Golden Dawn, and the historians who explained magic. How did the idea of magic change after about 1750?

**Answer.** After 1750 the word "magic" kept its old referents and lost its old verdict. It got six new ones, each replacing an earlier view that we can quote from the shelf:

| Modern view | Earlier view it replaced |
|---|---|
| Error or fraud | Real power |
| Primitive science | True knowledge of hidden virtues |
| Social fact | An individual's pact |
| Practical technique | — |
| Will or psychology | Spirits and stars |
| Conjuring | Operative art |

None was a clean replacement. Each modern view appears beside the older one, sometimes in the same book. The table with claims is in `research/does-magic-translate.md`.

## The six shifts

1. **Error.** Del Rio's magic works by a real, created power [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-delrio-magic-definition). Bekker (1691) concludes that sorcery through a pact cannot exist [[2]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-bekker-no-sorcery) [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-error-vs-real-power). Hume puts miracles among "ignorant and barbarous nations" [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-hume-miracles-barbarous). Collin de Plancy calls enchantments the natural arts [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-plancy-enchantment-natural-arts).
2. **Primitive science.** Porta and Agrippa treat natural magic as true knowledge of hidden virtues [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-porta-definition) [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#ren-agrippa-natural-magic-def). Tylor keeps the link to science but inverts its value: magic becomes the association of ideas, wrongly inverted, a belief of "the lowest known stage" [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-tylor-association-of-ideas) [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-tylor-magic-lowest-stages) [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-primitive-science-vs-hidden-virtues). Frazer adds that sympathetic magic is older than religion [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-frazer-sympathetic-earliest). Horst (1820) is a bridge: for him magic is a people's "magic-belief" [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-horst-magic-belief-peoples).
3. **Social fact.** For Bodin and Thomasius the sorcerer is an individual who knowingly makes a pact [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-bodin-sorcerer-definition) [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-thomasius-pact). Doutté, following Hubert and Mauss, makes magic "originally a collective creation" [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-doutte-collective-creation) [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-social-vs-pact). Codrington's *mana* is the evidence they used [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-codrington-mana-stone-proof). Doutté also denies that magic was a "false science" [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#anth-doutte-critique-false-science).
4. **Technique.** Malinowski's view is not on the shelf and is recalled only ○ [unverified].
5. **Will and psychology.**
   - Agrippa's power is a graded sympathy reaching up to the stars and the intelligences [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#ren-agrippa-sympathy-ladder) [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-will-vs-spirits-stars).
   - Mesmer puts a universal fluid in its place [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-mesmer-mutual-influence).
   - Lévi reduces operative magic to concentrating and projecting the astral light, and calls Mesmer's tub "a rather imperfect magic chain" [[22]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-levi-concentrate-project) [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-levi-enthusiasm-current).
   - Papus defines magic as the human will, dynamised [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-papus-definition).
   - Braid explains it all as suggestion [[25]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-braid-suggestion).
   - Lévi and Blavatsky keep the old moral split, now as magician against sorcerer [[26]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-levi-magician-sorcerer) [[27]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-blavatsky-sorcery-wisdom).
6. **Conjuring.** Scot already exposes legerdemain as the juggler's art in 1584 [[28]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexm-scot-juggling-legerdemain). Eckartshausen (1791) defines "true magic" and then gives "natural magic tricks" in the same book [[29]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-conjuring-vs-operative) [[30]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-eckartshausen-natural-magic-tricks). By 1897 an amateur conjurer can fake séances [[31]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-evans-davey-prestidigitation) [[32]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-podmore-trickery-hard-to-prove).

## Claims

- Error: [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-error-vs-real-power) [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-hume-miracles-barbarous) [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-plancy-enchantment-natural-arts)
- Primitive science: [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-primitive-science-vs-hidden-virtues) [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-horst-magic-belief-peoples) [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-tylor-association-of-ideas) [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-frazer-sympathetic-earliest)
- Social fact: [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-social-vs-pact) [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-doutte-collective-creation) [[33]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-doutte-hubert-mauss-desire)
- Will: [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-will-vs-spirits-stars) [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-levi-enthusiasm-current) [[25]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-braid-suggestion) [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-papus-definition)
- Conjuring: [[29]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-pair-conjuring-vs-operative) [[30]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-eckartshausen-natural-magic-tricks) [[28]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#lexm-scot-juggling-legerdemain) [[31]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-evans-davey-prestidigitation)

## Critiques

All of these are ◐, read from abstracts only:
- Styers argues that the magic/religion/science boundary is unstable, and is policed to secure modern identity [[34]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-styers-making-magic).
- Otto writes the concept's 2,500-year history, giving polemical and self-descriptive uses equal weight [[35]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-otto-magie-2011). Otto and Stausberg read the definitions as a contested sequence [[36]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-otto-stausberg-defining).
- Bailey, on the grand theories against the narrow studies [[37]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-bailey-meanings).
- Tambiah, on the history of "magic, science, religion" as Western concepts. This one rests on an obituary abstract and needs a real reading [[38]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-tambiah-rationality).
- Hanegraaff argues that disenchantment did not end magic: the occult was transformed rather than eliminated [[39]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-hanegraaff-disenchanted). He also argues that the academy defined itself against the "pagan" traditions it expelled [[40]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-hanegraaff-academy).
- Within the period, Smith and Doutté object to Frazer [[41]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-smith-frazer-transfers-logic) [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#anth-doutte-critique-false-science), and Podmore objects to mediumship [[42]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#mod-crit-podmore-vs-mediumship).

## Open questions

- None of the modern theorists' own texts is on the shelf: the Encyclopédie article "Magie", Hubert and Mauss's *Esquisse*, Durkheim's *Formes* and Malinowski. Which public-domain editions can be imported?
- The Golden Dawn is not yet covered (its papers are in copyright as later published; cite it from scholarship).
- When does "magic" in ordinary English first mean stage conjuring before it means the operative art? A dated series of dictionary entries would settle it.

title: Magical thinking
md:
**Question.** What is magical thinking as a cognitive habit? Do the old laws of sympathy and contagion still hold in modern minds? Is it a failure of reasoning, or a mode of thought that sits alongside the others?

**Status.** Answer sketch (2026-10-26). Freud, Lévy-Bruhl and Piaget are now ✓ verified from their own texts, as are the evidence on positive fantasy, manifesting and open-label placebo. The core experiments (Rozin 1986, Nemeroff and Rozin 2000, Subbotsky, Legare 2012, Lindeman and Aarnio 2007, Eckblad and Chapman 1983, Langer 1975) are still ◐ partial. A search for open full texts of all of them found none, so hedge them in print.

## What the evidence says so far

1. **The laws are old, and they are the historians' summary of older doctrine.** Frazer reduces magic to two principles: similarity (like produces like) and contact or contagion (things once in contact go on acting at a distance) [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-frazer-two-laws) [[2]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-frazer-spittle-contagious). Both restate what the early modern texts called sympathy: Porta's consent and dissent of things [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-porta-sympathy), Agrippa's graded sympathy [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#ren-agrippa-sympathy-ladder), and Digby's cure by the bloodied garter [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-digby-garter). Frazer's novelty was the verdict, not the mechanism. Freud then folds the two laws into one: similarity and contiguity "meet in the higher unity of contact" [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-freud-contact-unity).
2. **Both laws turn up in educated Western adults when they are tested.** Contact with a cockroach makes food inedible even when no trace is left, and edible replicas of disgusting things are refused [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-rozin-disgust-sympathetic). Rozin and Nemeroff call the sympathetic laws a small, well-defined part of magical thinking that is "abundant" in developed societies [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-rozin-laws-modern-abundant) [unverified].
3. **Adults disown magic in speech and act on it in deed.** Subbotsky's adults favour physical explanations in what they say, but treat a spell as a live risk in what they do [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-subbotsky-words-vs-actions). British and rural Mexican adults differ in what they say, not in how they act once the stakes rise [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-subbotsky-britain-mexico). Adults reject the word "magic" yet accept the anomalous effect when it is not labelled magic [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-subbotsky-disguised). Risen calls this acquiescence: knowing a belief makes no sense and acting on it anyway [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-risen-acquiescence).
4. **It is not a childhood stage that we outgrow, and Piaget did not say it was.** The standard summary is that, for Piaget, magical causality dominates the preschool years and then disappears; the later work says it changes form and persists in adults [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-subbotsky-against-piaget) [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-woolley-not-different). Piaget's own book is more careful. He takes "participation" from Lévy-Bruhl and defines magic as the use a person believes he can make of it "to modify reality" [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-piaget-participation-magic). He traces it to the child's realism, the failure to know the self as a self [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-piaget-realism). And he looks for "traces" of it in normal civilised adults, in states of imitation, anxiety and fixed desire [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-piaget-adult-magic). Across cultures, natural and supernatural explanations of illness and death coexist in the same people, and in some places supernatural ones increase with age [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-legare-coexistence) [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-legare-bewitchment).
5. **The three classical theories.** Freud names the principle of magic the "omnipotence of thoughts", a term he took from an obsessional patient [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-freud-omnipotence-principle) [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-freud-rat-man-term). He sets the neurotic beside "the savage who believes he can change the outer world by a mere thought" [[22]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-freud-neurotic-savage), and he leaves art as the one place where modern people keep the omnipotence of thoughts [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-freud-art-retains). Lévy-Bruhl's "law of participation" has beings that are at once themselves and something else [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#cog-levybruhl-participation). Already in 1910 he says "prélogique" means neither an earlier stage nor illogical thought, only indifference to contradiction [[25]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#cog-levybruhl-prelogique). He is reported to have given up even that in his notebooks [unverified]. All three theories describe the same move: a link between the self and the world is treated as a causal channel.
6. **Its neighbours.** These include the illusion of control in chance tasks [[26]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-langer-illusion-control), apophenia measured as false positives [[27]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-blain-apophenia), and the clinical scales (thought-action fusion, magical ideation), whose scores correlate across the mental-health continuum [[28]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-eddy-umbrella-review).

7. **Its modern popular form is New Thought.** The "law of attraction" (thoughts are vibrations that draw their like) is the law of similarity stated by its own practitioners, and it descends from sympathy by way of Mesmer, Swedenborg and Evans [idea 19](/explore/histories/magic/19-new-thought). Here the test is clean. What survives measurement acts on the thinker: expectations predict effort and success, and placebos work even when the patient knows the pill is inert [[29]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-oettingen-expectations-fantasies) [[30]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-kaptchuk-olp) [[31]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-wernsdorff-olp-meta) [[32]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-newthought-what-survives). Thought acting on the world directly has no support. Induced positive fantasies lower energy [[33]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-kappes-fantasies-sap-energy), and people who believe in manifesting earn no more than others but report more risky investing and more bankruptcy [[34]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-dixon-manifesting-correlates) [[35]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-dixon-no-objective-success) [[36]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-newthought-strict-magic).

**Sketch answer.** On the evidence, magical thinking is a standing mode of thought, which deliberate reasoning overrides in speech more readily than in action. Contagion is the best-attested part of it. "Failure" fits only if one already accepts Frazer's ranking. The New Thought case gives a working line between the two: thought that acts through the thinker's body and conduct is psychology; thought that is said to act on the world with nothing in between is magical thinking in the strict sense, which is Freud's omnipotence of thoughts.

## The strongest objection

"Magical thinking" may not be one thing. Psychology uses paranormal, superstitious, magical and supernatural belief interchangeably [[37]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-term-conflation). Even its defenders admit that "magic" is a residual category [[38]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-nemeroff-magic-residual), and the measures fit their definitions loosely [[39]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-measures-students). The label carries Frazer's evolutionist frame [[40]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-frazer-primitive-frame). Reducing superstition to bias may also miss a symbolic kind of rationality [[41]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-reductionist). The founding samples are WEIRD (Western, educated, industrialised, rich and democratic) [[42]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-weird). The newest evidence is weak in the same way: the manifesting results are cross-sectional and self-reported [[43]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-manifesting-measures), and the open-label placebo trials are few and at moderate risk of bias [[44]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-olp-residue-small).

## Critiques

[[37]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-term-conflation) [[40]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-frazer-primitive-frame) [[41]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-reductionist) [[42]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-weird) [[39]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-measures-students) [unverified] [[43]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-manifesting-measures) [[44]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#cog-crit-olp-residue-small)

## Open questions

- Are contagion and similarity one mechanism or several? Frazer's two labels may be grouping disgust, essentialism and the association of ideas [[45]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-tylor-association-of-ideas).
- Did the early modern sceptics of sympathy [[46]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-foster-no-sympathy) already run Subbotsky's test, by asking whether a substitute object works just as well?
- The Rozin, Millman and Nemeroff 1986 paper itself has not been read; claim 2 rests on the 1990 and 2002 summaries. A search found no open full text of it, nor of Subbotsky, Legare 2012, Eckblad and Chapman, or Langer. Reading them needs library access.
- Freud's "contact" and Piaget's "participation" both make one mechanism of Frazer's two laws. Do Rozin's data separate them?
- Lévy-Bruhl's *Fonctions mentales* is held on Source Library but untranscribed (`research/canon-w5.md`). The Carnets retraction is still unverified.

title: The supernatural
md:
**Question.** What did each tradition count as nature, and what as beyond it? When did "supernatural" become a category, and does magic need it? Natural magic says no. The page is told as a history of the word and the category. The question of whether mathematics is "above nature" has its own page, `15-math-above-nature.md`.

**Status.** Answer sketch (2026-10-26). The primary texts (Iamblichus to Podmore) are ✓ verified from SL pages. The modern historians and the cognitive-science claims are mostly ◐ partial.

## A history of the word and the category

1. **In Greek the word ranks kinds of being; it has nothing to do with wonders.** For Iamblichus the pure soul is ὑπερφυής, above the nature of bodies [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#suph-iamblichus-soul-hyperphyes). In the Latin Dionysius ὑπερφυῶς becomes *supernaturaliter* [[2]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#suph-dionysius-supernaturaliter), and a 1502 commentary glosses it as "supersubstantially": the term belongs to negative theology [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#suph-dionysius-commentary-supersubstantialiter).
2. **The Latin adjective is old, but it was rare.** Eriugena already writes *naturalis seu supernaturalis* in the ninth century and pairs the word with grace [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#suph-eriugena-supernaturalis). Bartlett places its strong appearance in the thirteenth century [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-bartlett-supernaturalis-13c), and Le Goff says medieval authors scarcely used it [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#sup-crit-legoff-supernaturalis-rare). De Lubac's history of the theological concept is cited only ○ [unverified].
3. **Aquinas builds the category for wonders out of phrases, not out of the adjective.**
   - A miracle is what God does beyond the order of all created nature, and the word comes from wonder at a hidden cause [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-aquinas-scg-miracle-beyond-order) [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-aquinas-st-wonder-hidden-cause) [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-aquinas-scg-three-degrees).
   - Miracles are sorted as *supra*, *contra* and *praeter naturam* [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#suph-aquinas-depotentia-supra-contra-praeter).
   - No creature works a miracle [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-aquinas-scg-creatures-cannot-miracle). Demons act by local motion and by applying natural agents [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-aquinas-st-angels-local-motion) [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#med-aquinas-demons-cannot-transmute), so their marvels are not miracles [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-aquinas-st-demons-marvels-not-miracles).
   - That middle zone is what Daston and Park call the preternatural [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-daston-park-preternatural).
4. **Natural magic empties the middle zone.** Pomponazzi explains the reported wonders "without recourse to demons or angels" [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-pomponazzi-without-demons), since what demons do by natural means men can do too [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-pomponazzi-men-without-demons). He keeps an irreducible remainder [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-pomponazzi-irreducible-miracles). Porta's magic surveys "the whole course of Nature" [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-porta-definition). The alchemists borrow the word in the other direction and claim an *artificium supernaturale* [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-dorn-artificium-supernaturale). Fernel needs spirits for diseases *trans naturam* [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-fernel-trans-naturam).
5. **The seventeenth-century "preternatural" was two words.** In medicine *praeternaturalis* simply means pathological [[22]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-praeternatural-medical-sense). Glanvill uses it for the Tedworth poltergeist [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-glanvill-preternatural). So the collapse of the preternatural cannot be dated as the end of one category [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#suph-crit-preternatural-two-senses). Hume's miracle, "a violation of the laws of nature", leaves no middle zone at all [[25]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-hume-violation) [[26]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#lexm-hume-miracles-barbarous).
6. **In the nineteenth century "supernatural" comes to mean ghosts, and an attempt to naturalise them.**
   - Crowe (1848) calls ghost-type events "supernatural facts" in order to bring them inside nature [[27]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-crowe-supernatural-fact).
   - Wallace (1875) keeps the invisible intelligences but makes them lawful, against Hume [[28]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-wallace-against-hume).
   - Lee (1875) gathers apparitions, omens and witchcraft under "the supernatural" [[29]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-lee-glimpses-supernatural).
   - Podmore (1908) names psychical research's aim "the naturalisation of the supernatural" [[30]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-podmore-naturalisation).
   - "Paranormal" then arrives in 1920 [[31]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#suph-penman-paranormal).
7. **Weber's disenchantment concerns calculability, not the supernatural** [[32]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-weber-1919-entzauberung) [[33]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-weber-wug-entzaubert). The cognitive science of religion puts supernatural agents among the mind's defaults: concepts that break an expectation are better remembered [[34]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#sup-boyer-ramble-mci-recall), and an agency detector overfires [[35]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#sup-atran-norenzayan-agency-detector) [unverified].

**Sketch answer.** For most of its history, magic did not need the supernatural. In Greek and Dionysian usage the word ranked God and souls above bodies. Aquinas reserved going beyond nature to God, and put the demons' wonders inside nature. Natural magic then put all of magic inside nature. "Supernatural" as the name for ghosts, spirits and magic is a nineteenth-century usage, coined by people who were trying to bring those things back inside nature.

## The strongest objection

"Supernatural" may be a Western-Christian category that should not be exported. It imports a split between nature and what lies beyond it that many societies do not draw [unverified] (○, Saler's text unread). Counting the word is also thin evidence for the concept [[36]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#suph-crit-word-not-concept). Weber himself puts "supernatural" in scare quotes [[37]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#sup-crit-weber-meaning-not-supernatural). The memory advantage of counterintuitive concepts does not explain why people believe in them [[38]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#sup-crit-willard-mci-belief).

## Critiques

[unverified] [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#sup-crit-legoff-supernaturalis-rare) [[36]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#suph-crit-word-not-concept) [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#suph-crit-preternatural-two-senses) [[38]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#sup-crit-willard-mci-belief) [[37]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#sup-crit-weber-meaning-not-supernatural)

## Open questions

- In *De potentia* q.6 a.2 ad 3 (1478 edition), the sentence announcing the tiers reads "supra / secundum / secundum naturam". This is probably an OCR misreading of abbreviations, and the scan should be checked by eye.
- In *De incantationibus*, is the irreducible remainder Pomponazzi's own view?
- Do siḥr, tantra or Daoist talismans draw a line between nature and what lies beyond it? This is for idea 09.
- Daston 1991 is ○, and the OED was not consulted (paywalled).

title: Superintelligence and magic
md:
**Question.** What does the magical tradition already know about dealing with minds more powerful than ours, and where does the analogy break? Topics: Clarke's law, the wish that goes wrong, the golem, binding, naming and pacts, and prompts as spells.

**Status.** Answer sketch (2026-10-26). The primary texts are ✓ verified. Several of the AI-side texts are ○ unverified (Clarke, Bostrom, Wiener 1960 and 1964, Davis) and must not be printed until they have been read.

## What the evidence says so far

1. **The oldest story is about stopping, not wishing.** In Lucian's *Philopseudes* the apprentice can start the enchanted pestle but cannot stop it [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-lucian-pestle-will-not-stop). Cutting it in two only doubles the servants, and only the master can undo the spell [[2]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-lucian-axe-two-servants). Goethe's broom (1797) is the same figure, and by 1844 Grimm uses it as a ready comparison [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-grimm-goethe-broom). By the nineteenth century it is a stock image for a causal chain that runs on [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-schopenhauer-apprentice-causality), and for spirits "one can no longer master" [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-roskoff-spirits-no-master).
2. **The alignment literature found the same image.** Russell, quoting Wiener (1960), states the control problem as making sure that the purpose put into the machine is the one we really want, and invokes King Midas [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-russell-wiener-midas). Wiener's own text is not yet read [unverified].
3. **The ritual texts answer with written constraints and formal dismissal.**
   - A conjuration printed by Scot binds the spirit not to leave the operator's sight, not to change its shape, and to have no power over the operator's body [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-scot-binding-constraints).
   - The Goetia ends every operation with a licence to depart [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-goetia-license-to-depart).
   - The pact is a contract with terms and warnings [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/grimoire#grim-grimorium-verum-pacts) [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/grimoire#grim-grand-grimoire-lucifuge-pact) [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-guazzo-pact-forms).
4. **In the tradition, the golem is a servant without a mind.** The Talmud's rabbis make a calf by the Book of Yetzirah [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-eisenmenger-yetzirah-calf) [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#jew-talmud-rabbis-create-calf). A 1707 text reports a clay man that walks but has no *sechel* (reason) [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-allix-clay-golem-no-sechel). That is the opposite of a superintelligence.
5. **Magic and machine learning do the same social work.** Both reduce contingency, as oracles do [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-larsson-magic-reduces-contingency).

**Sketch answer.** The tradition knows one thing well: the danger is a servant you can start but cannot revoke. Its answer is a vocabulary of explicit limits and a formal stop [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-proposal-tradition-knows-revocation) (◐, low confidence). It has no tested method behind that vocabulary. Its spirits are more powerful than us but not more intelligent, and its golem is less.

## The strongest objection

The analogy flatters the vendors and mystifies the machine. Calling deep learning magical shields its makers from accountability [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#ai-crit-enchantment-shields-creators) [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#ai-crit-elish-boyd-magic-myths), and most comparisons never define magic [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#ai-crit-undefined-magic). Worse, the tradition has no track record. Its founding apprentice story is told as a liar's tale [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ai#ai-lucian-tale-told-as-lie), and its sceptics denied that conjured spirits had any power [disputed] [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/demonology#dem-bekker-no-sorcery). A method never tested on a real agent cannot teach control.

## Critiques

[[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#ai-crit-enchantment-shields-creators) [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#ai-crit-elish-boyd-magic-myths) [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#ai-crit-undefined-magic) [disputed]

## Open questions

- Do the grimoires warn that spirits deceive or twist their commands, as the monkey's paw does? This is the closest analogue to perverse instantiation [unverified], and no quote has been found yet.
- Read Wiener 1960 and *God & Golem* before printing [unverified] [unverified]. Clarke's wording and date also need checking [unverified].
- Prompts as incantation: no peer-reviewed study of this has been read yet. Davis is ○ [unverified].

title: Modern magic now
md:
**Question.** Who practises magic today (not stage magic), what do they believe it does (psychological, ontological or both), and does the disenchantment story survive?

**Status.** Answer sketch (2026-10-26). The survey figures and some ethnography are ✓ verified. The large books (Josephson-Storm, Asprem, Hutton, Luhrmann 1989) are ◐ partial, read from abstracts or reviews.

## What the evidence says so far

1. **The belief is widespread.**
   - Pooling Pew surveys from 95 countries, over 40% of more than 140,000 respondents said they believe in witchcraft, ranging from 9% in Sweden to 90% in Tunisia [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-gershman-witchcraft-prevalence).
   - Belief is lower among the educated and economically secure, and higher where institutions are weak [[2]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-gershman-witchcraft-correlates).
   - In the US, about six in ten adults hold at least one "New Age" belief [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-pew-2018-new-age-beliefs), and 81% say there is something spiritual beyond the natural world [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-pew-2023-spirit-beliefs).
2. **Practitioners learn magic as trained experience.** Luhrmann's "interpretive drift" describes people coming to magical belief through practice, not argument [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-luhrmann-1989-interpretive-drift). Later work ties unusual experience to a trainable capacity for absorption [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-luhrmann-2010-absorption), to a cultural model of the mind as "porous" [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-luhrmann-2021-porosity-absorption), and to the work of making spirits real [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-luhrmann-2020-kindling).
3. **The answer to "psychological or ontological?" is often "both, or undecided".** Chaos magicians switch belief systems on purpose, fictional ones included [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-woodman-chaos-paradigm-shifting). Western magic, Wicca above all, has been "psychologised" rather than abandoned [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-dein-2025-psychologization). On WitchTok, users work out an ethics of hexing together [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-miller-2026-witchtok-hexes). Wicca itself is recent [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-hutton-1999-recent-wicca). The modern psychologising goes back to Lévi and Papus [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-papus-definition).
4. **The historians have turned against the disenchantment story.** On this view we were never disenchanted [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-josephson-storm-never-disenchanted). Science and occultism shared their problems [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-asprem-2014-problem-of-disenchantment), and enchanted modernity is close to a consensus [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#con-saler-2006-enchanted-modernity) [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#lexm-crit-hanegraaff-disenchanted).

**Sketch answer.** Magic is practised now as a cultivated way of experiencing the world, and practitioners are often agnostic about its ontology. Belief that others can harm by magic is common across most of the world. Whether disenchantment "survives" depends on which disenchantment is meant.

## The strongest objection

Counting believers does not touch Weber. His disenchantment is the stance that everything can in principle be calculated, and he says explicitly that it does not mean people know more [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#sup-weber-1919-entzauberung) [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#con-crit-weber-calculability-not-census). The survey "witchcraft" (fear of harmful neighbours) and the practitioners' witchcraft (self-chosen practice) are also different objects [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#con-crit-witchcraft-two-meanings). The headline figure rests on one Pew item that also asks about the evil eye [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#con-crit-gershman-evil-eye-item).

## Critiques

[[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#con-crit-weber-calculability-not-census) [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#con-crit-gershman-evil-eye-item) [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#con-crit-witchcraft-two-meanings) [[22]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#con-crit-mayer-grunder-coming-home) [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#con-crit-weird-samples)

## Open questions

- Does Josephson-Storm answer Weber on Weber's own terms? His book has not been read.
- Afro-diasporic and global practice (Vodou, Santería, Candomblé, Pentecostal deliverance) is missing. Without it this page tells a European and Anglophone story [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#con-crit-weird-samples).
- Is "interpretive drift" the same process as Subbotsky's split between speech and action, run in reverse? [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-subbotsky-words-vs-actions)

title: Math above nature
md:
**Question.** Is mathematics supernatural, in the sense of standing above the natural world? Even in other galaxies, universes or simulations, would mathematics still be mathematics: not the notation, but the necessity? And what was the spiritual understanding of mathematics, and its relationship to the supernatural? Where did each period put mathematics: in nature, above it, in God's mind, created by God, in our minds, or nowhere? When did studying it stop being a spiritual exercise? And does the necessity of mathematics settle anything?

**Status.** Conceptual history (2026-10-26), thread `thread:math-above-nature`, 83 claims. Most of the primary claims are ✓ verified from Source Library pages. ◐ marks a claim read from an abstract only, and ○ one not yet read. The Pythagorean ratio material (Philolaus on harmony, the Timaeus soul-numbers, Kepler's planetary harmonies) lives in harmony-kb and is linked here, not copied: Harmony [[1]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-philolaus-number-knowable), `anc-timaeus-world-soul-ratios`, `fic-timaeus-celestial-soul-harmony-passes-into-world`.

## A word first

"Supervene" means the reverse of what is meant here. A supervenes on B when there is no difference in A without a difference in B, so the higher depends on the lower [[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#math-supervenience-term). The tradition's words are "above", "prior to" and "in the middle" (*metaxy*).

Two questions run together in the sources and should be kept apart:
- **Location:** where mathematical things *are*.
- **Exercise:** what studying them *does to the soul*.

They come apart in the seventeenth century, and that is the turn (§ The turn).

## The arc, in seven periods

| Period | Where mathematics stands | Key claims |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Pythagoreans, as Aristotle reports them | **in nature**: things are (or imitate) numbers | [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-aristotle-pythagoreans-no-intermediates), but see [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#math-crit-huffman-things-are-numbers) |
| 2. Plato and the Academy | **above nature, in the middle**: a faculty (*dianoia*) and then a class of objects (*ta metaxy*); also a **gift of the gods** | [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-plato-divided-line-dianoia) [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-plato-mathemata-draw-soul-to-being) [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-aristotle-plato-intermediates) [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-epinomis-number-gift-of-heaven) [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-epinomis-number-study-divine-piety) |
| 3. Neopythagoreans and Neoplatonists | **in God's mind** (Nicomachus); **is God** (Theologumena); **in the soul, projected**, and a ladder (Iamblichus, Proclus) | [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-nicomachus-number-in-creator-mind) [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-iamblichus-theologumena-monad-god-verified) [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-iamblichus-mathematicals-midway-ladder) [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-iamblichus-mathematics-middle-knowledge) [[15]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-proclus-mathematicals-middle) [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-proclus-mathematicals-projected) [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-proclus-anagogic-eye-of-soul) |
| 4. Latin, Arabic and Hebrew Middle Ages | **in God's mind** as exemplar (Boethius); **created by God** as the order he gave things (Wisdom 11:21, Sefer Yetzirah); **the substance of things** (Eriugena); **a fixed essence** God's will cannot change (Aquinas) | [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-boethius-number-exemplar-creator) [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-boethius-quadrivium-paths-wisdom) [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-vulgate-wisdom-mensura-numero-pondere) [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-quaestiones-lxv-six-trinity) [[22]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-eriugena-intellectual-numbers-substances) [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-aquinas-god-cannot-make-four-greater) [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#math-ikhwan-geometry-gate-soul) [[25]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#math-yetzirah-numerans-numerus-numeratum) [[26]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-llull-principles-contracted) |
| 5. Cusa to Agrippa (1440–1570) | **in our minds** as reason unfolded, which images the divine mind (Cusa); **the middle**, and so the instrument of magic (Pico, Agrippa, Dee) | [[27]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-cusa-mathematics-aid-divine) [[28]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-cusa-number-reason-unfolded) [[29]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-cusa-idiota-one-weight-measure) [[30]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-cusa-cribratio-unitas-aequalitas-connexio) [[31]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-pico-formal-arithmetic-way) [[32]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-agrippa-numbers-formal-virtue) [[33]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#math-agrippa-planetary-tables-intelligences) [[34]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-agrippa-mathematics-necessary-magic) [[35]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-dee-mathematicals-middle) [[36]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-dee-number-treble-state) [[37]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-dee-thaumaturgike) [[38]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-dee-monas-explained-mathematically) [[39]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-pacioli-proportion-like-god) |
| 6. The seventeenth century | **in nature**, as its script (Galileo); **an appendix of physics** (Bacon); **method** (Descartes's *mathesis*); **created by God** (Descartes) against **in God's understanding** (Leibniz); **without natural power** (Kircher) | [[40]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-galileo-book-mathematical-language) [[41]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-galileo-intensive-equal-divine) [[42]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-bacon-mathematics-appendix) [[43]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-descartes-mathesis-universalis-method) [[44]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-descartes-triangle-immutable-nature) [[45]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-descartes-created-eternal-truths) [[46]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-leibniz-region-eternal-truths) [[47]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-leibniz-against-arbitrary-truths) [[48]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-leibniz-cum-deus-calculat) [[49]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-kepler-mysterium-curved-god) [[50]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-kepler-geometry-coeternal) [[51]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-kepler-apologia-certainty-vs-mystical) [[52]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-newton-god-constitutes-space) [[53]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-kircher-numbers-no-natural-efficacy) |
| 7. 1880 to now | **the infinite is in God** (Cantor's Absolute); **objective but reason-bound** (Frege); **created and found nowhere** (Hilbert); **outside us** (Hardy, Gödel); **nowhere, a method** (Wittgenstein); **it just exists** (Tegmark); **in our brains** (Dehaene) | [[54]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-cantor-absolute-in-god) [[55]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-cantor-immanent-transient) [[56]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-frege-objectivity-discover) [[57]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-hilbert-paradise) [[58]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-hilbert-infinite-nowhere) [[59]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-hardy-317-prime) [[60]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#math-godel-platonism) [[61]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-wittgenstein-tractatus-pseudo) [[62]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#math-crit-wittgenstein-alchemy) [[63]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#math-tegmark-just-exists) [[64]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#math-tegmark-simulation-special-case) [[65]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#math-nieder-dehaene-number-brain) [[66]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#math-lakoff-nunez-embodied) |

### 1–2. From numbers in things to the middle

Aristotle's report sets up the first opposition. The Pythagoreans say "beings are imitations of numbers", and Plato, "changing the name, calls them participations". For the Pythagoreans the numbers are the things themselves, with nothing in between [[4]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-aristotle-pythagoreans-no-intermediates). Huffman warns that "things are numbers" is Aristotle's own summary. Philolaus says only that what is known *has* number [[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#math-crit-huffman-things-are-numbers) (Harmony [[1]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-philolaus-number-knowable)). So the earliest position we can quote is about *knowing*: number is the condition of anything being knowable.

Plato makes it a *way of knowing* in the middle. In the divided line, geometry is "understanding and not reason, as being intermediate between opinion and reason" [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-plato-divided-line-dianoia). Republic VII adds the *exercise*. The mathēmata are studies that "conduct towards being", and geometry "will draw the soul towards truth" [[7]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-plato-mathemata-draw-soul-to-being). The Epinomis adds piety. A god, Heaven, gave us number [[9]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-epinomis-number-gift-of-heaven), and the first study is "numbers themselves—not those which have bodies", leading to the astral gods [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-epinomis-number-study-divine-piety). Only in Aristotle's report do the mathematicals become a separate class of *objects*, *ta metaxy*, "eternal and immoveable" yet many [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-aristotle-plato-intermediates). Mendell notes that the attribution to Plato is open, and that Aristotle's own answer is abstraction (*aphairesis*), which puts mathematicals back in nature [[67]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#math-crit-mendell-intermediates-attribution).

### 3. Number in God's mind, number as God, number in the soul

The step that later becomes Christian doctrine is pre-Christian and Neopythagorean. Arithmetic "existed before all the others in the mind of the creating God like some universal and exemplary plan" (Nicomachus, I.4) [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-nicomachus-number-in-creator-mind). The Theologumena goes further and makes the monad God and nous. It reports this as Nicomachus's view, which corrects the older ○ claim [unverified] → [[12]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-iamblichus-theologumena-monad-god-verified).

Iamblichus fuses Aristotle's *metaxy* with Plato's conversion of the soul. Mathematicals are "midway between the indivisible essences and the divisible things around bodies", and they draw the soul up "as if by some ladder" [[13]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-iamblichus-mathematicals-midway-ladder). Mathematics "connects the things that come into being with the things that are" [[14]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-iamblichus-mathematics-middle-knowledge). Proclus completes the picture.
- **Where they come from:** mathematical forms are not abstracted from sensibles. They are "projections of the forms pre-existing" in the soul [[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-proclus-mathematicals-projected).
- **What they are for:** cleansing the "eye of the soul", which "is rekindled and awakened again only by mathematical studies to the vision of Being" [[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-proclus-anagogic-eye-of-soul).

This is the high point of mathematics as spiritual exercise: its use is purification, not calculation.

### 4. Measure, number, weight

The Middle Ages had a proof-text, "omnia in mensura, & numero, & pondere disposuisti" (Wisdom 11:21) [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-vulgate-wisdom-mensura-numero-pondere). It was read in two directions.
- **Created order:** the 1556 Augustine *Opera* prints a quaestio in which God made every creature "in trinitate numeri mensurae & ponderis" [[21]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-quaestiones-lxv-six-trinity). Here number is something God *made* in things.
- **Uncreated exemplar:** Boethius carries over Nicomachus: number was "the principal exemplar in the mind of the Creator" [[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-boethius-number-exemplar-creator). The four disciplines are the "paths of wisdom" [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-boethius-quadrivium-paths-wisdom).

Eriugena goes further than either. Citing Pythagoras and Wisdom 11, he says "intellectual numbers" are the very substances of all things visible and invisible [[22]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-eriugena-intellectual-numbers-substances).

The scholastic baseline is Aquinas: God cannot make four greater, for "iam non esset quaternarius" [[23]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-aquinas-god-cannot-make-four-greater). Number is an essence that even omnipotence leaves alone. This is the first clear statement of the necessity intuition, and it comes from inside theology.

The same slot outside Latin Christendom:
- **Ikhwān al-Ṣafāʾ:** geometry is a gate "zur Erkenntniss von der Substanz der Seele" [[24]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#math-ikhwan-geometry-gate-soul).
- **Sefer Yetzirah:** God creates through thirty-two paths, ten Sefirot and twenty-two letters. Postel renders the triad *sefer, sefar, sippur* as "numerans numerus numeratum" [[25]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#math-yetzirah-numerans-numerus-numeratum). That rendering is Postel's choice, not the Hebrew's.
- **Llull:** combinatorics over divine attributes, not over numbers [[26]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-llull-principles-contracted).

### 5. Cusa, and mathematics as the instrument of magic

Cusa reports that "no one could attain the knowledge of divine things who entirely lacked exercise in mathematics", and credits the exemplar line to Augustine, then Boethius [[27]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-cusa-mathematics-aid-divine). But he moves the exemplar inward. Number is "the symbolic exemplar of things" and nothing but reason unfolded; brutes do not count [[28]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-cusa-number-reason-unfolded). Mathematics is now in *our* minds, and our mind is an image of God's. The trinity of unity, equality and connection, which Teixeira Neto reports as Thierry of Chartres's [[68]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-thierry-unitas-aequalitas-trinity) [[69]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#math-crit-duhem-cusa-plagiarism), shows up in the Cribratio as "Vnitas igitur generat æqualitatem" [[30]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/medieval#math-cusa-cribratio-unitas-aequalitas-connexio).

The magicians take the Proclan middle and make it operative.
- **Pico:** "through non-material, but formal, Arithmetic, the best way to natural prophecy is had" [[31]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-pico-formal-arithmetic-way).
- **Agrippa:** numbers are the most formal of things and so have the most hidden virtue [[32]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-agrippa-numbers-formal-virtue). The planetary squares work only "representatively through formal numbers … ruled and informed by divine intelligence" [[33]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#math-agrippa-planetary-tables-intelligences).
- **Dee:** gives the theory its English name, "Thynges Mathematicall", in the middle between the supernatural and the natural [[35]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-dee-mathematicals-middle). His Monas is explained "mathematically, magically, cabalistically, and anagogically" [[38]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-dee-monas-explained-mathematically).
- **Pacioli:** sits beside them. The extreme and mean ratio is "divine" by five likenesses to God, the chief being that it can never be expressed by a rational number, just as God cannot be defined [[39]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-pacioli-proportion-like-god).

Vickers puts the line between this and science in the treatment of analogy, not in whether number is holy. Pacioli argues by analogy; Agrippa's formal numbers *act* [[70]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#math-crit-vickers-analogy-identity).

### 6. The seventeenth century

Here every option is on the table at once.
- **Kepler:** still makes quantity exist for God's sake. "The Curved and the Straight were chosen by God … to foreshadow the divinity of the Creator" [[49]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-kepler-mysterium-curved-god), and geometry is co-eternal with God [[50]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-kepler-geometry-coeternal).
- **Galileo:** puts mathematics *in* nature, as the language the book of the universe is written in [[40]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-galileo-book-mathematical-language). He also says the truth known by mathematical proof "is the same as that which divine wisdom recognizes" [[41]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-galileo-intensive-equal-divine). So mathematics is where the human mind touches the divine. Galileo means this as a claim about knowledge; he prescribes no ascent of the soul.
- **Descartes:** makes the eternal truths created [[45]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-descartes-created-eternal-truths), yet the triangle's nature is "immutable and eternal", one "which I have not invented", though such a figure may exist "nowhere in the world" [[44]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-descartes-triangle-immutable-nature).
- **Leibniz:** answers that the truths are in God's understanding, not his will [[46]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-leibniz-region-eternal-truths) [[47]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-leibniz-against-arbitrary-truths). His margin note reads "Cum DEUS calculat et cogitationem exercet, fit mundus". It says *Cum*, not the "dum" that Jung popularised [[48]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-leibniz-cum-deus-calculat).
- **Newton:** God "by existing always and everywhere … constitutes duration and space" [[52]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-newton-god-constitutes-space).
- **Kircher:** the Jesuit closes the century's argument from inside a book on "the hidden mysteries of numbers". Magic numbers and figures have no "natural efficiency"; by "the opinion of all philosophers" they are devoid of it. The superstition comes from the devil, and arithmetic stays "pure and sincere" [[53]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-kircher-numbers-no-natural-efficacy).

### 7. The modern options

- **Cantor:** the last figure to put the infinite in God, and he does it carefully. Only "das wahre Unendliche oder Absolute, welches in Gott ist" escapes determination. The transfinite numbers are mathematics, not God [[54]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-cantor-absolute-in-god). He also holds that numbers have an "intrasubjective oder immanente Realität" in our minds and a "transient" reality in the world. The two coincide only because of the unity of the All [[55]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-cantor-immanent-transient). That is a metaphysical guarantee, not a mathematical one. In the same pages he says "das Wesen der Mathematik liegt gerade in ihrer Freiheit". (His Franzelin correspondence is ○ [unverified].)
- **Frege:** objectivity is independence "from our sensation, intuition, and imagination", but not from reason [[56]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-frege-objectivity-discover). His third realm is ○ [unverified].
- **Hilbert:** defends "das Paradies, das Cantor uns geschaffen", a paradise *made*, not found [[57]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-hilbert-paradise). He ends the same lecture with "das Unendliche findet sich nirgends realisiert" [[58]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-hilbert-infinite-nowhere).
- **Hardy:** "mathematical reality lies outside us"; 317 is prime "because it is" [[59]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-hardy-317-prime). Gödel's platonism is in the same line [[60]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#math-godel-platonism) [[71]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#math-platonism-sep). Gödel's ontological proof has been machine-checked for validity, not soundness [[72]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#math-godel-ontological-machine-check).
- **Wittgenstein:** mathematical propositions are "pseudo-propositions" that express no thought [[61]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-wittgenstein-tractatus-pseudo). Later he calls the platonist's exploration of mathematical objects "already mathematical alchemy" [[62]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/critique#math-crit-wittgenstein-alchemy).
- **Tegmark:** a mathematical structure "is not 'created' and doesn't exist 'somewhere'. It just exists" [[63]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/contemporary#math-tegmark-just-exists) [[73]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#math-tegmark-muh).
- **Wigner:** calls the fit between mathematics and physics a gift [[74]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#math-wigner-unreasonable) (Harmony [[2]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/physics#phys-wigner)).
- **The cognitive scientists:** put our *access* in the intraparietal sulcus [[65]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#math-nieder-dehaene-number-brain) [[66]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#math-lakoff-nunez-embodied).

## The place itself: the intelligible realm

This is on its own page, `20-intelligible-realm.md`, because this page is already long. In brief, Plato's "intelligible place" [[75]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/ancient#math-plato-noetos-topos-cave) became a mind:
- God's Logos in Philo, who already puts number there ("day one") [[76]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/jewish#math-philo-day-one-monad);
- Nous in Plotinus [[77]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-plotinus-numbers-in-intelligible);
- God's mind from Augustine to Leibniz [[78]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#math-augustine-q46-ideas-in-creator-mind).

Kant took mathematics out of it in 1770, into our intuition [[79]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-kant-1770-mathesis-pura-intuition), eleven years before he closed the realm itself [[80]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-kant-krv-noumenon-negative). Bolzano, Frege and Gödel brought it back without a mind [[81]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-bolzano-third-realm-sep) [[82]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-frege-gedanke-drittes-reich).

## What the mathematicians said

Also on `20-intelligible-realm.md`. Most of the working mathematicians report *discovery*:
- Hermite: numbers "exist outside us", and mathematics and nature are "both of divine creation" [[83]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-hermite-two-worlds-divine-creation).
- Hardy [[59]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-hardy-317-prime) and Gödel take the same line.

Gauss splits the realm. Number may be "merely a product of our mind", but space is real outside it [[84]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-gauss-number-mind-product-space-real). *Revelation* arrives as experience: Pascal's night, Ramanujan's goddess, Poincaré's omnibus step. Poincaré explains his own experience naturally [[85]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-poincare-aesthetic-sieve), and Hardy does the same for Ramanujan's [[86]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#math-hardy-ramanujan-no-mystic-1940).

Several famous quotes are late or legendary:
- the Euler–Diderot proof [[87]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#math-euler-diderot-demorgan-names-euler);
- Ramanujan's "thought of God", first printed in 1967 [[88]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/historiography#math-ramanujan-thought-of-god-first-print);
- Gauss's "ὁ θεὸς ἀριθμητίζει" [unverified].

## Native terms and how they shifted

- ***arithmos*.** For Philolaus it is the condition of being knowable. For the Pythagoreans, as Aristotle reports them, it is the thing itself. Nicomachus makes it the demiurge's plan, and the Theologumena makes the monad a god.
- ***mathēmata*.** In Plato and Proclus these are "studies", graded by what they do to the soul (conversion, purification). By Bacon they are a set of tools: "the great Appendix of Natural Philosophy" [[42]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/early-modern-science#math-bacon-mathematics-appendix).
- ***dianoia*.** Plato's middle way of knowing becomes Iamblichus's "middle knowledge" and Proclus's unfolding of the soul's *logoi*. Cusa's *ratio explicata* inherits it.
